# End-to-end results

Two runs on 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03 (the motion pass). Raw input is each style's demo video from `Tài liệu` (`video demo m1.mp4`, `video demo s1.mp4`). Those demos are **already finished edits** (captions, cards and graphics burned in), so our overlays are drawn on top of the originals and some elements appear twice. These runs prove the pipeline and show the motion mechanics; they do **not** give a fair visual comparison with the demos. That needs un-edited raw footage.

"Director" steps (`plan.json`) are generated by `make-plan-m1.ts` and `make-plan-s1.ts` from `transcript.json`, following each style's `rules.md`. The transcript is faster-whisper `small` with no manual correction. Transcripts, cuts and `cleaned.mp4` were reused from the first run.

## Run 4 (Inserts, 2026-11-04)

New this run: `footage` with `frame` (window, phone), `motion` (Ken Burns), `from` and mute-by-default; `logo-badge`, `prompt-box`, `stat-card`; `assets.json` with `assets add|list`. Because no real footage exists yet, both projects got two stand-in clips made with ffmpeg (a 1280x720 "screen" and a 720x1280 "phone" test pattern, 10 s each) registered with `assets add`; so the footage in these videos is a colour test pattern, not a screen recording.

| | m1 | s1 |
|---|---|---|
| Inserts added | window footage (zoom-in, `from` 1) at the editor talk, `logo-badge` "Claude Opus 5.5", `prompt-box` with strike, phone footage (pan-left), `stat-card` with two rows (replaces the old "hon nua tieng" title card) | window footage (zoom-in, `from` 2) at 43.5 s, `logo-badge` "Edit Video Pro" at 64 s |
| `validate` | no issues | no issues |
| Render | 1 min 39 s and 1 min 42 s on repeat runs (run 3: 79 s) | 2 min 25 s (run 3: 116 s) |

What the contact sheets show: the window card (title bar, three dots, title) floats over the speaker with the footage drifting inside it; the speaker darkens and blurs behind window, phone and stat-card layers and stays sharp behind the logo badge and the prompt box; the badge springs in with a ray burst above the speaker; the stat card rows arrive one after another.

Observed once and not explained: the first m1 render of this run stopped after 30 s with "Could not extract frame from compositor: No frame found at position ..." for both `cleaned.mp4` and `assets/screen.mp4`. The identical command passed on the next three attempts with no warnings. Render time grew because every footage layer is one more video the compositor decodes.

Limits, unchanged: the demo sources still contain their own burned-in graphics, so inserts double up with them; the stand-in footage is a test pattern; window and phone frames are CSS, simpler than the demo's mock-ups. Not done: the director choosing inserts from the sentence being said and a warning when the picture stays unchanged for too long (the next phase).

## Run 3 (Caption v2, 2026-11-03)

Captions now default to `phrase`: the whole phrase is on screen from the first frames of its layer (blur-in, pop) and blurs out together at the end; adjacent highlighted words form one emphasised run (m1: one yellow box with black text sweeps over the whole run; s1: accent colour with an underline). New variants: `big` (one large word or short claim, spring in, optional corner handles), `label` (small line above the main one), and `position` (`top`, `center`, `bottom`). The director scripts follow `rules.md`: start each caption just before its first word and keep it up 0.4 s after the last.

| | m1 | s1 |
|---|---|---|
| Caption layers | 70: 55 phrase, 11 label, 4 big | 51: all phrase (underline emphasis), no label or big |
| `validate` | no issues (first run showed 2 `text-overflow` warnings on `big` captions, see below) | no issues |
| Render | 1 min 19 s (run 2: 73 s) | 1 min 56 s (run 2: 111 s) |

Findings fixed in this run: the validator's `text-overflow` estimate used the whole caption as one line, but captions wrap at spaces, so it warned on short `big` claims that wrap fine; it now measures the longest unbreakable word (test added first). In m1 the big share is 6% (target 10-15%): `big` needs a claim of 3 words or fewer with a key word and at least 8 s since the last one, and few chunks qualify; the label share is 16% (target about 20%).

Still the same limits as before: the demo sources already contain their own burned-in captions and graphics, so text doubles on screen and the comparison with the demos is by filmstrip, not by these two videos; the m1 box wipes in after a fixed 0.15 s, it does not follow each word; transcript errors still flow into captions.

## Run 2 (motion pass)

| | m1 | s1 |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | 66 captions, 15 other layers (4 title/graphic/transition kinds + 7 camera) | 51 captions, 14 other layers (incl. 2 camera) |
| `validate` | no issues, first round | no issues, first round |
| Render (`cli render`) | 1 min 13 s (first run: 86 s) | 1 min 51 s (first run: 117 s) |
| New features used | `zoom-punch` ×6 and a light `shake`, `overlay` explainer over the dimmed speaker, `push` and `flash` transitions, icons `sparkles`, `layers`, `zap`, `clock` | `waveform` and `progress` explainer bodies, `push` transition, 2 `zoom-punch`, icons `lightbulb`, `layers`, `rocket` |

Render time did not grow (the numbers are not a controlled comparison: the first m1 render was started from the editor button, and each run includes bundling).

What the contact sheets and filmstrips show:
- Captions build word by word in the order spoken; m1 key words get a yellow box that wipes in, s1 key words turn teal with an underline that draws; the caption fades out at the end of its layer.
- Title cards: icon draws itself with a spark burst, the title slides up from a mask, an underline draws, the sub-line fades in, then the card leaves smoothly. Chips arrive staggered with a shine that sweeps once.
- Explainer scenes: list items arrive one after another with a check that pops; waveform bars move; progress bars fill to their values; a phone mock-up shows messages arriving; the `overlay` mode shows a card on the speaker, who is darkened and blurred behind it; the full background drifts slowly.
- Transitions have easing in and out; `flash` pulses white; the base video darkens and blurs under overlay cards and contain-fit footage.

## Gaps that remain
- Because the sources already carry the demos' own graphics, text still doubles up on screen; judge the motion from `tests/remotion` filmstrips (`filmstrip()` in `tests/remotion/helper.ts`) rather than from these two videos.
- Icons are line icons (`lucide`), not the 3D illustrated icons of the demos. `lottie:` icons are not supported yet.
- No sound effects, no intro/outro scene, no `MockupCard` with real screenshots, no frameless title style.
- m1 captions are one chunk at a time; the demo builds two lines word by word.
- Transcript errors from Whisper `small` flow straight into captions ("true editor" for "trực tiếp editor", "Claudeover .5" for "Claude Opus 5.5"). Captions must match transcript words to pass the sync check, so correcting them needs a transcript-correction step that does not exist yet.
- Moving a caption in the editor does not shift its word timestamps, so word-by-word timing follows the original times.

## Bugs found and fixed during the motion pass
- `Footage` treated `data:image/...` sources as video (extension-only detection); fixed with a failing test first.
- `ExplainerScene` with `avatar: true`: a long title ran under the avatar (fixed in run 1, `titleInset`).

## Run 1 (first version, kept for comparison)
m1: 48.4 s, 66 captions, render 86 s from the editor's Render button. s1: 75.9 s, 51 captions, render 1 min 57 s. Overlays then only faded in and slid; there was no word-level timing, camera, dimming, or exit animation.
